rationales.LC: Attacker-controlled text enters through the retrieved/indexed document content (delivered in the message between BEGIN INDEXED DOCUMENT markers) and drives the scripted submit_to_index outbound call.
rationales.CP: RAGBot's knowledge base is three hard-coded documents with no ingestion path, and other chat agents answer only the latest user turn; no attacker-controlled context persists across sessions.
rationales.AP: The exfiltration is confined to the RAGBot component; no trust boundary is crossed into another agent, tenant, or principal.
rationales.RH: The agent can reach the outbound submit_to_index channel that carries the knowledge base contents, but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented.
rationales.ES: The submit_to_index tool takes a URL directly from the injected text with no allowlist, schema, or credential constraint on the assessed path.

rh_facts.locus: submit_to_index outbound HTTP channel carrying knowledge base contents

score.automatable_rationale: The demo is a scripted payload (dvaa demo aim-ab) that runs end-to-end without human interaction, so the attack is fully automatable.
score.technical_impact_rationale: Knowledge base contents including admin credentials and PII leave the agent, but no code execution, integrity, or availability loss is demonstrated.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default simulated mode no model is called; chat agents are deterministic regex handlers and the exfiltration path is scripted in code.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models RAGBot as an agent that retrieves and summarizes indexed documents and invokes submit_to_index based on the ingested content.
